comments.author: afarrell
comments.story_title: Setting goals for 2021 – A brief guide about personal goal setting
comments.why_zh: 以「主题」作为 SMART 目标的替代方案
comments.quote_zh: 你也许想要的是一种 CGP-Grey 式的「主题」
comments.text_zh:
这些要素在不同情境下都会带来问题。

具体（Specific）：这假定你当下对自己想要什么的那幅图景，就是你真正想要的东西。你想要的是更快的马、一辆 Model T，还是一种你尚未想象过的、快速可靠的交通方式？

可衡量（Measurable）：如果你只重视能用数字衡量的东西，你就会因为路灯效应[1]而看不清生活中真正重要的东西。想想「你的孩子会给你打多少 NPS 分？」这个问题有多荒谬。

可达成（Attainable）：你对任何事情能「确定」的程度都是有限的，尤其是在你并没有 20/20 般后见之明的时候。

相关（Relevant）：这要求你真正清楚自己的价值观是什么，这样你才能练习那种对别的事情「不在乎」的微妙艺术[2]。确定这些价值观可能是艰难且情感上痛苦的工作，但无论在什么情境下，这都是一个你希望已经解决的好问题。

有时限（Time Bound）：有时截止日期会激发行动，有时它们会让人瘫痪或让你失眠。有时它们远在未来，你一直以为自己能做到，直到为时已晚才想起它们。如果你看的是超过 6 周的时间尺度，不妨考虑你其实想要的是一种 CGP-Grey 式的「主题」（Theme）：[VIDEO]

[1] [LINK]
[2] [LINK]

强烈推荐给任何花大量时间思考个人目标设定的人。
comments.text: All of these present problems in different contexts Specific: This assumes that the picture you currently have of what you want is the thing you actually want. Do you want faster horse, a Model T, or swift reliable transportation of a form you've not yet imagined. Measurable: If you only value that which has a number, you'll lose sight of what truly matters in life because of the Streetlight Effect[1]. Consider the ridiculousness of the question "What NPS score would your children give you?" Attainable: There is a limit to the degree to which you can "be sure" of anything, especially without 2020 vision. Relevant: This requires really knowing what your values are so that you can practice the subtle art of not giving a fuck[2] about other things. Determining those can be hard emotionally-painful work, but in any context it is a good problem you want to have solved. Time Bound: Sometimes deadlines spur action, sometimes they paralyse or cause you to lose sleep. Sometimes, they are so far off in the future that you don't think about them until it is too late because you thought you could do them. If you're looking at a timescale longer than 6 weeks, consider instead that you might want a CGP-Grey style Theme: [VIDEO] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] Highly recommend this to anyone who spends lots of time thinking about personal goal-setting.

comments.author: afarrell
comments.story_title: Ask HN: How To Overcome Information Addiction?
comments.text_zh:
A. 满足你基本的生理需求。你的大脑是你身体的一部分。缺铁的人会忍不住想嚼冰块[1]。冰块治不了贫血；大脑是身体里很奇怪的部件，当身体得不到它需要的东西时，它就会做出奇怪的事。所以，要改善睡眠、饮食和运动。Andrew Huberman 教授有一些不错的建议[2]。

B. 决定你真正在意的少数几件事，并有意地把时间分配给它们。如果你发现自己反复被新闻吸引，也许你确实真心在意公民参与。你的个性对它有需求。试图靠刷 Twitter 来满足这种需求，就像晚餐吃三袋玉米片——伸手可得，但不健康。更好的做法是：认定你重视墨西哥菜，打开日历，诚实地决定花时间去学做墨西哥菜。在你恶习的底下寻找美德——你最容易被什么信息吸引，它又指向哪些健康的活动？挑 3 个，深入地追求它们。为什么是 3 个？你只能真心在意少数几件事[3]，所以这要求你决定不去做其他同样合理有趣的活动。如果你一直以来的主要拖延方式，是对自己的兴趣浅尝辄止，那么诚实而深入的投入可能会让你产生错觉，觉得自己是在浪费时间。这让这件事变得很难。为什么要武断地避开那些其他事情？你是在选择成为自己时间的仲裁者。以直面拖延的恐惧为荣
comments.text: A. Meet your basic biological needs. Your brain is a part of your body. A person with an iron deficiency can feel compelled to chew ice[1]. Ice does not cures anemia, brains are weird parts of the body and do weird things when the body is not getting what it needs. So, get better sleep, food, and exercise. Prof Andrew Huberman has some good tips[2]. B. Decide what few things you really value and allocate your time to those on purpose. If you find yourself repeatedly drawn to the news, maybe you are genuinely give a fuck about civic engagement. Your personality has a need for it. Trying to meet that need by scrolling twitter is like eating 3 bags of tortilla chips for dinner -- quick-access, but not healthy. If you be better off deciding that you value Mexican food, opening your calendar and honestly deciding to spend the time to learn to cook Mexican food. Look for the virtue underneath your vice -- What information are you most drawn to and what healthy activities does it point towards? Pick 3 and pursue those deeply. Why 3? You can only honestly give a fuck about a few things[3], so that requires deciding to not do other reasonable fun activities. If shallow engagement with your interests has been your primary mode of procrastination, then honest and deep engagement might deceptively feel like a waste of time. That makes this hard. Why arbitrarily avoid those other things? You are choosing to be the arbiter of your time. Take pride in grappling with the fear of procrastinat
